marco: Heads-up 10: we're trying to finalize the private-deploy networking strategy for the upcoming release. Need a single recommended default for customers and a clear upgrade story. Quick takes?

anya: Default should bias toward the least-op-infrastructure option so customers can get started fast. I'm thinking: 1) Relay mode = default (no routing required), 2) Static NAT for customers who need IP preservation, 3) BGP as opt-in enterprise feature.

kevin: Agreed on ordering. Relay reduces support surface. But we need to spell out tradeoffs: relay increases egress hop and L7 proxying, NAT preserves egress but breaks source IP continuity for inbound flows. BGP preserves both but needs Ops coordination.

samir: From infra: implementability timeline: Relay + operator install = 2 sprints. Static NAT via customer gateway + config template = 1 sprint more. BGP onboarding with templates + validation checks = 4-5 sprints, plus docs.

olivia: Can we make a simple customer-facing decision tree so field SEs can recommend the right mode? Eg: "Do you need your egress IP preserved? -> Yes: NAT or BGP. Do you control edge routers? -> Yes: BGP." We should ship that with the installer.

marco: Good. We also need clear upgrade choreography. Options: small rolling upgrades with abort on >5% error, or staged blue/green that requires dual-path networking during cutover. Which is our default?

anya: Rolling upgrades as default. It's less demanding on customer infra. For customers who demand sub-second failover we'll offer guidance + runbook for blue/green.

kevin: Agree. Add a safety net: an automated canary that routes 2% of traffic to new version for 15 minutes and runs smoke checks. If smoke fails, abort and roll back. Keep config tunable via `redwoodctl rollout set --canary 2 --window 15m`.

samir: Speaking of `redwoodctl`, I'll add flags: `--preflight-only`, `--target-mode=[relay|nat|bgp]`, and a machine-readable JSON exit code for CI integration. Example: `redwoodctl install --preflight-only --output=json` returns {"status":"ok","checks":[]}.

olivia: Please ensure preflight covers: firewall ports, MTU mismatch detection, kernel network stack (nftables vs iptables), and whether customer has provider NAT that would conflict with static egress IPs.

kevin: We'll also add a minimal BGP sample snippet in docs so SEs can copy-paste. Example config (vendor-agnostic pseudo):

```bgp
neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65001
neighbor 10.0.0.1 ebgp-multihop
network 198.51.100.0/24
```

marco: Nice. On telemetry: legal said default must be opt-out at least for perf/error metrics for early access customers; but product prefers default OFF. Any resolution?

anya: Let's compromise: default OFF for public hosted customers, default OFF for private deploy unless customer picks "managed telemetry" option during install. For early partners, we can enable ON through signed consent in SE onboarding.

samir: We'll implement `redwoodctl telemetry status` and `redwoodctl telemetry consent --scopes=errors,latency`. Consent will print a human-readable summary and produce a signed token for audit.

olivia: Field asks: include a recommended "maintenance window" template for customers. Suggest wording: "Planned upgrade may require up to 60 minutes; rolling upgrades will minimize downtime but network-level changes may need coordination." Put that in installer and RFC.

kevin: Also call out blockers in preflight: legacy load balancers (F5 with SNAT), private DNS records that point to egress IPs, and strict ACLs that only allow old IPs. Add a checklist item for each.

marco: Action items: Samir to spec `redwoodctl` flags & JSON outputs (due Tue), Kevin to draft preflight checklist and BGP sample (due Wed), Olivia to draft decision tree doc and maintenance window template (due Wed), Anya to prepare the customer comms copy for field (due Thu). I'll assemble RFC Friday morning.

infra-bot: Created ticket PD-5123 "private-deploy networking defaults + rollout plan" assigned to @marco, @samir, @kevin, @olivia, @anya.

anya: One last thing 12: for NAT mode, provide a recommended HA setup for the NAT gateway so customers don't introduce a single point of failure. Small diagram in docs should do it.

marco: Good call. We'll add a HA reference architecture with two NAT gateways + healthcheck + failover IP. End sync.
thread_text_summary: Coordination thread to finalize private-deploy networking defaults: relay default, NAT for egress preservation, BGP enterprise opt-in; rolling upgrades with canary; redwoodctl flags & preflight checklist; telemetry defaults and customer comms; action owners assigned
